$comment: T2.9/T3.2 (PLAN-ci-time-budget, operator spec W). Measured cost per lane, read by
scripts/ci-runner/lanes.ts's shardPlan (its optional 4th argument) so a sharded lane
balances legs by real duration once one exists, instead of by scheduler `weight`.
'jobs' is each job's fixed cost (p90 minutes, setup through the first runner step);
'units' is each shard-plan unit id's own p90 in MILLISECONDS, keyed exactly as the
id appears in gates.lock.json (a quality-code check id) or in a test lane's own
enumerator (scripts/ci-runner/unit-enumerators.ts), for example 'pytest:tests/....py'.
SEEDED 2026-09-26 with 'concurrency' only (operator ruling D-W1: stay on GitHub Free,
20 concurrent jobs) -- 'jobs' and 'units' are empty until T3.2's
'budget_report.py --refresh' runs against real green CI data. An empty 'units' means
every shardPlan caller falls back to `weight` for every unit, so quality-code's plan
is unaffected until this file actually names one of its ids (see the selftest control
'shardPlan(durations: {}) is byte-identical to shardPlan() with no durations argument'
in scripts/gate-bind.ts).
T3.1's freshness check (scripts/gates/check-lane-budget.ts) reds when the TOP-LEVEL
'refreshed_at' is older than 14 days -- that field, plus 'jobs'/'units'/'defaultUnitMs',
is written ONLY by 'budget_report.py --refresh' (T3.2/T3.3).
'job_max_seconds' is a SEPARATE section, D-W2/T3.4's retirement of the old
job-timeout-baseline.json into this one file: check_job_timeout_headroom.py's own
baseline for the two direct (never lane-sharded) ci.yml jobs the lane-budget gate does
not cover, Validate Promotion and Stage Artifacts. It carries its OWN 'refreshed_at',
written ONLY by 'check_job_timeout_headroom.py --refresh' -- a shared timestamp would
let either refresh silently un-stale numbers the other half never re-measured.
'job_max_seconds.jobs[*].observed_max_seconds' is the worst observed wall time in
SECONDS (MIN_HEADROOM=1.5x that number must fit under the job's timeout-minutes),
migrated verbatim from job-timeout-baseline.json's last real refresh (run 32491717875,
see that retired file's own history for the full 'why one sample' account).
'defaultUnitMs' (hand-authored 2026-09-28, T3.1; --refresh preserves it verbatim). The
quality lanes price their units by gate id, and no test-runner artifact reports a gate
id, so these lanes carry one MEASURED per-unit figure each instead of per-gate p90s.
Source: the Actions jobs API (paginated; every job, not the first 100) for the 10 latest
completed pull_request runs of ci.yml, 36332829873..36370123947 (2026-09-27T16:19Z to
2026-09-28T02:31Z), success-only jobs as budget_report samples them. Derivation per lane:
defaultUnitMs = (p90 job wall minutes - jobs[lane] fixed minutes) x 60000 / unit count,
and for sharded quality-code the MAX of that over its 4 legs (leg 1: 8.8m / 23 units),
so no leg is priced below its own measurement. A lane with no 'jobs' entry has its fixed
cost folded into the figure (fixed 0 in the gate). Inputs, p90 wall / units: branch
8.5m / 9 (completed jobs: the job fails every PR run on check:ci-plan-implementation,
so it has no success sample), code legs 8.8/6.2/7.5/6.4m / 23/27/27/27, content
3.0m / 45, gate-tests 0.8m - 0.7m fixed / 6, go 7.6m / 17, i18n 5.1m / 40, packages
5.7m / 13, security 1.8m / 18, static 4.5m / 64, wiring 0.5m / 1, www-build 3.6m / 16.
NOT given one, on purpose: quality-pytest and test-renet-integration HAVE measured unit
p90s, but budget_report keys them by junit classname ('pytest:/ci/...',
'renet-integration:TestX.py') where the committed manifests say 'pytest:.ci/...' and
'renet-integration:test_x.py', so none of them match; a lane default there would bury
that keying defect instead of surfacing it. These figures are not refreshed by any
tool yet: re-derive them by the recipe above when refreshed_at moves.
